Kiln gearbox running hot or shaking
The main gearbox that turns the kiln is heating up or vibrating more than usual. A bearing may be wearing or the gearbox may be short of good oil.
Outside air leaking in at the kiln feed end
There is more oxygen at the kiln inlet than expected, so outside air may be getting in past the seal where the turning kiln meets the fixed inlet chamber. Fuel is wasted and the flame can change.

Burner air fan running hot or shaking
The fan that blows the air shaping the burner flame (primary air fan) has a bearing heating up or is vibrating more than usual.
Ground coal in the bin is getting warmer or giving off carbon monoxide (CO). It may be starting to smoulder, which can lead to a fire or an explosion.
Coal flow to the burner blocking or weakening
Less coal is reaching the kiln burner than set, or the pressure in the coal line is changing. The flame can weaken and the kiln cool down.
The flame at the kiln burner looks longer, shorter or less steady than usual. A changed flame can damage the kiln lining and make clinker of poor quality.
The conveyor that carries clinker to the silo is drawing more current than usual or its chain is slowing down or stopped.
The crusher motor is drawing more current than usual or the crusher is slowing down. Large lumps or metal may be stuck in it.
Clinker crusher bearing running hot or shaking
A bearing on the crusher's hammer rotor is heating up or vibrating more than usual.
Clinker silo dust filter clogged or torn
The pressure difference across the filter bags on the clinker silo is too high or too low. Bags may be clogged with dust or torn and letting dust out.
Cooling fan running hot or shaking
A cooling fan's bearing is heating up or the fan is vibrating more than usual.
Cooler grate jammed or losing hydraulic power
The hydraulic pressure that moves the cooler grate is rising or falling, or the grate is moving slower than set. Hot clinker can pile up at the cooler inlet.
Clinker leaving the cooler too hot
Clinker coming out of the cooler is hotter than usual. Hot clinker can damage the crusher and conveyor, and the heat it carries is lost.
Cooler exhaust fan dirty or wearing
The fan that draws dusty air out of the cooler is vibrating more, heating up or drawing more current than usual.
Feed elevator drive running hot or shaking
The drive at the top of the bucket elevator (lifts raw material up to the preheater) is heating up or vibrating more than usual.
Feed elevator slowing down or stopping
The bucket elevator that lifts raw material up to the preheater is turning slower than usual, or its motor is working harder while it moves less material.
Kiln feed rate unsteady or the feed meters disagree
The amount of raw meal going to the kiln jumps up and down, or the two feed flow meters show different amounts.
Raw meal not flowing out of the feed silo
The feed silo is not emptying as it should: its level stays the same or the kiln feed bin runs low while the kiln is being fed.
Kiln drive working harder than usual
The main kiln motor needs more power than usual to turn the kiln at the same speed. Something may be rubbing or dragging, or material may be building up inside.
Kiln ring gear and its drive gear wearing
The small drive gear that turns the big ring gear around the kiln is vibrating more than usual. The gear teeth may be wearing or not getting enough lubricant.
Kiln support roller bearing running hot
A bearing on one of the rollers that carry the kiln is getting hotter than the others. It may be short of oil or cooling, or the roller may be carrying too much load.
Hot spot on the kiln shell
Part of the kiln's steel shell is hotter than the rest. The brick lining or the protective coating inside may be missing there, and the steel can be damaged if it stays hot.
Fuel not burning completely in the calciner
Carbon monoxide (CO) is rising at the calciner outlet or the preheater exit, so some fuel is not burning fully. This wastes fuel and can make the exhaust gas unsafe.
Raw meal may be building up in one of the lower cyclones (the hottest stages of the preheater tower). The pressure in its cone changes and hot meal stops flowing down to the kiln.
Outside air leaking into the preheater
There is more oxygen at the top of the preheater than lower down, so outside air may be getting in. The exhaust fan then has to work harder and fuel is wasted.
Exhaust fan running hot or shaking
The exhaust fan that pulls hot gas through the kiln and preheater has a bearing heating up or is vibrating more than usual.
Cooling water too warm or flowing too little
The cooling water for the melting coil is flowing less than usual or warming up more as it passes through the machine. The coil can overheat and the heater will cut out.
Vacuum pump struggling to pull the vacuum
The vacuum pump takes longer than usual to empty the air from the mould chamber, or the chamber does not reach its usual low pressure. Castings can come out with holes or not fill.
